title: Prime Numbers, Factors, Multiples, LCM and HCF
seo_title: Prime Numbers, LCM and HCF – Primary 5 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Identify prime numbers up to 100; find factors and multiples; find the LCM and HCF of numbers; solve problems on LCM and HCF. (summary of the NERDC Primary 5 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Primary 5 maths worksheets on prime numbers, factors and multiples, the lowest common multiple (LCM) and the highest common factor (HCF), with word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: A prime has exactly two factors
key_sub: LCM: smallest shared multiple. HCF: biggest shared factor.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A factor divides a number exactly. A multiple is in the number's times table.
  • A prime number has exactly two factors: 1 and itself (2, 3, 5, 7, 11, …). 1 is not prime.
  • LCM is the smallest number that is a multiple of each number. HCF is the biggest number that is a factor of each number.

Examples

Example

LCM of 6 and 8

Multiples of 8: 8, 16, 24

24 is a multiple of 6

Answer: 24

Example

HCF of 18 and 24

Factors of 18: 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18

6 also divides 24

Answer: 6

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Calling 1 a prime number1 has only one factor, so it is not prime.
Mixing up LCM and HCFLCM is big (a multiple); HCF is small (a factor).
Thinking all odd numbers are prime9, 15 and 21 are odd but not prime.

faq.a: Yes. It is the only even prime.
When things happen together again, such as two bells that ring at different times.
When we cut or share things into the largest equal groups.

items.q: Which list shows all the factors of 12?
items.e: Find the factor pairs: 1 × 12, 2 × 6, 3 × 4. So the factors are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12. Do not forget 1 and 12, and do not miss 3 × 4. 12, 24, 36, 48 are multiples of 12, not factors.

items.q: Which list shows all the factors of 20?
items.e: Find the factor pairs: 1 × 20, 2 × 10, 4 × 5. So the factors are 1, 2, 4, 5, 10, 20. Do not forget 1 and 20, and do not miss 4 × 5. 20, 40, 60, 80 are multiples of 20, not factors.

items.q: Which list shows all the factors of 24?
items.e: Find the factor pairs: 1 × 24, 2 × 12, 3 × 8, 4 × 6. So the factors are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24. Do not forget 1 and 24, and do not miss 3 × 8. 24, 48, 72, 96 are multiples of 24, not factors.

items.q: Which list shows all the factors of 30?
items.e: Find the factor pairs: 1 × 30, 2 × 15, 3 × 10, 5 × 6. So the factors are 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 10, 15, 30. Do not forget 1 and 30, and do not miss 5 × 6. 30, 60, 90, 120 are multiples of 30, not factors.

items.q: This array shows 18 dots. Which factor pair of 18 does it show?
items.e: There are 3 rows of 6 dots: 3 × 6 = 18. So 3 × 6 is a factor pair of 18. 2 × 9 is another pair, but it is not the one shown, and 3 + 6 = 9, not 18.
There are 4 rows of 7 dots: 4 × 7 = 28. So 4 × 7 is a factor pair of 28. 2 × 14 is another pair, but it is not the one shown, and 4 + 7 = 11, not 28.

items.q: Which of these is a factor pair of 36?
items.e: 4 × 9 = 36, so 4 and 9 are a factor pair. 6 × 5 = 30, 3 × 13 = 39 and 2 × 16 = 32. The other pairs of 36 are 1 × 36, 2 × 18, 3 × 12 and 6 × 6.

items.q: The factor rainbow shows all the factors of 24. Which number is missing?
items.e: The arc joins ? to 3, so 3 × ? = 24. 24 ÷ 3 = 8. 21 is 24 − 3, not 24 ÷ 3. 9 and 7 are not factors of 24.

items.q: The factor rainbow shows all the factors of 30. Which number is missing?
items.e: The arc joins ? to 2, so 2 × ? = 30. 30 ÷ 2 = 15. 28 is 30 − 2, 60 is 30 × 2, and 10 is already in the rainbow (it pairs with 3).

items.q: Which number is not a factor of 32?
items.e: 32 ÷ 6 = 5 remainder 2, so 6 is not a factor of 32. 4 × 8 = 32. 8 × 4 = 32. 16 × 2 = 32.

items.q: Which number is not a factor of 45?
items.e: 45 ÷ 6 = 7 remainder 3, so 6 is not a factor of 45. 3 × 15 = 45. 9 × 5 = 45. 15 × 3 = 45.

items.q: Which number is not a factor of 56?
Which number is a factor of 42?
items.e: 7 × 6 = 42, so 7 is a factor of 42. 84 is a multiple of 42, not a factor, and 8 and 12 leave a remainder.

items.q: Which number is a factor of 54?
items.e: 9 × 6 = 54, so 9 is a factor of 54. 108 is a multiple of 54, not a factor, and 8 and 12 leave a remainder.

items.q: How many factors does 16 have?
items.e: The factor pairs are 1 × 16, 2 × 8 and 4 × 4. The factors are 1, 2, 4, 8, 16: 5 factors. 4 × 4 uses 4 only once, so do not count it twice (6). 3 is the number of pairs.

items.q: How many factor pairs does 24 have?
items.e: 1 × 24, 2 × 12, 3 × 8 and 4 × 6. That is 4 factor pairs. 8 is the number of factors, not pairs.

items.q: Hauwa lists the factor pairs of 48: 1 × 48, 2 × 24, 3 × 16, 6 × 8. Which pair did she miss?
items.e: Test 1, 2, 3, 4 … in order. 48 ÷ 4 = 12, so 4 × 12 is missing. 8 × 6 is the same pair as 6 × 8. 5 × 10 = 50 and 7 × 7 = 49, not 48.

items.q: Which number has exactly 3 factors?
items.e: The factors of 9 are 1, 3 and 9: 3 factors (3 × 3 counts 3 once). 6 has 4 factors (1, 2, 3, 6), 7 has 2 (1, 7), and 12 has 6.

items.q: Chidi says 7 is a factor of 27 because 27 has a 7 in it. Is he right?
items.e: 7 × 3 = 21 and 7 × 4 = 28, so 27 is not in the 7 times table. 27 ÷ 7 = 3 remainder 6, so 7 is not a factor. The digits do not matter. 27 is not prime either: 27 = 3 × 9.

items.q: What is the largest factor of 35 that is less than 35?
items.e: The factors of 35 are 1, 5, 7 and 35. The largest one below 35 is 7. 34 is 35 − 1, and 35 ÷ 2 is not a whole number, so 17 is not a factor.

items.q: Which of these is a prime number?
items.e: 13 has exactly two factors, 1 and 13, so 13 is prime. 15 = 3 × 5, so 15 is not prime. 21 = 3 × 7, so 21 is not prime. 1 has only one factor, so it is not prime.

items.q: Which number is not a prime number?
items.e: 1 has only one factor, so it is not prime. 2, 3 and 5 are prime: each has exactly two factors. 2 is prime, even though it is even.

items.q: Which list shows all the prime numbers up to 19?
items.e: The primes up to 19 are 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19. Learn them by heart. 1 is not prime, 2 is prime, 9 = 3 × 3 and 15 = 3 × 5 are not prime, and do not leave out 19.

items.q: Is 51 a prime number?
c: Yes. It has only two factors
items.e: Test small primes. 5 + 1 = 6, which is in the 3 times table, so 51 divides by 3: 51 = 3 × 17. So 51 is not prime. Being odd does not make a number prime, and 5 × 11 = 55.

items.q: Which number is composite?
items.e: A composite number has more than two factors. 39 = 3 × 13, so 39 is composite. 2 and 37 are prime. 1 is neither prime nor composite: it has only one factor.

items.q: How many factors does a prime number have?
items.e: A prime number has exactly two factors: 1 and itself. 7 has factors 1 and 7. A number with more than two factors is composite.

items.q: How many prime numbers are there between 20 and 30?
items.e: The odd numbers are 21, 23, 25, 27, 29. 21 = 3 × 7, 25 = 5 × 5 and 27 = 3 × 9, so only 23 and 29 are prime: 2 primes. Counting every odd number gives 5, and 3 or 4 means a number like 21, 25 or 27 was counted.

items.q: Bola says every odd number is prime. Which number shows she is wrong?
items.e: 15 is odd, but 15 = 3 × 5, so it is not prime. 15 shows the rule is wrong. 13 and 11 are odd and prime, so they fit the rule, and 2 is not odd.

items.q: Halima says 2 is not a prime number because it is even. Is she right?
items.e: The factors of 2 are 1 and 2, so 2 is prime. It is the only even prime: every other even number divides by 2.

items.q: Chinedu says 1 is a prime number. Is he right?
items.e: A prime number has exactly two factors: 1 and itself. 1 has only one factor, so it is not prime. It is not composite either.

items.q: Which shows 12 as a product of prime factors?
items.e: Keep splitting until every branch ends in a prime: 12 = 2 × 2 × 3. 3 × 4 is not finished, because 4 is not prime. 1 is not prime, so it is not written. 2 × 3 = 6, not 12.

items.q: Which shows 18 as a product of prime factors?
items.e: Keep splitting until every branch ends in a prime: 18 = 2 × 3 × 3. 3 × 6 is not finished, because 6 is not prime. 1 is not prime, so it is not written. 2 × 3 = 6, not 18.

items.q: Which shows 40 as a product of prime factors?
items.e: Keep splitting until every branch ends in a prime: 40 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 5. 5 × 8 is not finished, because 8 is not prime. 1 is not prime, so it is not written. 2 × 5 = 10, not 40.

items.q: What are the prime factors of 42?
items.e: 42 = 2 × 3 × 7, and 2, 3 and 7 are all prime. So the prime factors are 2, 3 and 7. 1 is not prime, 6 = 2 × 3 and 21 = 3 × 7.

items.q: Which number is a prime factor of 35?
items.e: 35 = 5 × 7, and 7 is prime, so 7 is a prime factor. 35 is a factor but not prime, 1 is not prime, and 3 is prime but not a factor of 35.

items.q: What is 2 × 2 × 3 × 5?
items.e: 2 × 2 = 4, 4 × 3 = 12, 12 × 5 = 60. So the prime factors of 60 are 2, 2, 3 and 5. 12 comes from adding, 30 uses only one 2, and 120 uses three 2s.

items.q: Babatunde says every odd number is prime. Which number shows he is wrong?
items.e: 15 is odd, but 15 = 3 × 5, so it is not prime. 15 shows the rule is wrong. 13 and 11 are odd and prime, so they fit the rule, and 2 is not odd.

items.q: Simi says 2 is not a prime number because it is even. Is she right?
items.e: The factors of 2 are 1 and 2, so 2 is prime. It is the only even prime: every other even number divides by 2.

items.q: Emeka says 1 is a prime number. Is he right?
items.e: A prime number has exactly two factors: 1 and itself. 1 has only one factor, so it is not prime. It is not composite either.

items.q: Ifeanyi says every odd number is prime. Which number shows he is wrong?
items.e: 15 is odd, but 15 = 3 × 5, so it is not prime. 15 shows the rule is wrong. 13 and 11 are odd and prime, so they fit the rule, and 2 is not odd.

items.q: Which number is a multiple of 6?
items.e: 6 × 7 = 42, so 42 is a multiple of 6. 16 ÷ 6 = 2 remainder 4. 26 ÷ 6 = 4 remainder 2. 63 ÷ 6 = 10 remainder 3. Having a 6 as a digit does not make a number a multiple of 6.

items.q: Which number is a multiple of 8?
items.e: 8 × 9 = 72, so 72 is a multiple of 8. 28 ÷ 8 = 3 remainder 4. 18 ÷ 8 = 2 remainder 2. 84 ÷ 8 = 10 remainder 4. Having an 8 as a digit does not make a number a multiple of 8.

items.q: Which number is a multiple of 9?
items.e: 9 × 9 = 81, so 81 is a multiple of 9. 19 ÷ 9 = 2 remainder 1. 39 ÷ 9 = 4 remainder 3. 89 ÷ 9 = 9 remainder 8. Having a 9 as a digit does not make a number a multiple of 9.

items.q: Which number is not a multiple of 7?
items.e: 7 × 6 = 42 and 7 × 7 = 49, so 47 is not in the 7 times table. 7 × 7 = 49, 7 × 8 = 56 and 7 × 5 = 35.

items.q: What is the 6th multiple of 8?
items.e: The 6th multiple of 8 is 8 × 6 = 48. 40 is the 5th multiple, 56 is the 7th, and 14 is 8 + 6.

items.q: Which list shows the first five multiples of 4?
items.e: The multiples of 4 are 4 × 1, 4 × 2, 4 × 3 …: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20. The first multiple is 4 itself. 1, 2, 4 are the factors of 4.

items.q: Sani shades the multiples of 3 on this number track. Which multiple of 3 has he missed?
items.e: Count in 3s: 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18. 3 × 5 = 15 is not shaded. 13 has a 3 as a digit, but 13 ÷ 3 = 4 remainder 1. 16 and 10 are not multiples of 3.

items.q: Gbenga says 30 is a factor of 5. Is he right?
items.e: 5 × 6 = 30, so 30 is a multiple of 5, and 5 is a factor of 30. A factor divides the number; a multiple is in its times table.

items.q: Which statement is true?
items.e: 7 × 8 = 56, so 7 is a factor of 56 (and 56 is a multiple of 7). 56 ÷ 6 = 9 remainder 2, so 6 is not a factor of 56.

items.q: Which list shows all the common factors of 12 and 16?
items.e: Factors of 12: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12. Factors of 16: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16. The numbers in both lists are 1, 2, 4. Remember 1, and use only numbers that divide both.

items.q: Which list shows the first 3 common multiples of 4 and 6?
items.e: Multiples of 6: 6, 12. Multiples of 4: 4, 8, 12. The first number in both lists is 12. The common multiples are the multiples of the LCM: 12, 24, 36. Counting in 4 × 6 = 24s skips 12.

items.q: Which list shows the first 3 common multiples of 6 and 9?
items.e: Multiples of 9: 9, 18. Multiples of 6: 6, 12, 18. The first number in both lists is 18. The common multiples are the multiples of the LCM: 18, 36, 54. Counting in 6 × 9 = 54s skips 18.

items.q: Which list shows the first 3 common multiples of 10 and 12?
items.e: Multiples of 12: 12, 24, 36, 48, 60. Multiples of 10: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60. The first number in both lists is 60. The common multiples are the multiples of the LCM: 60, 120, 180. Counting in 10 × 12 = 120s skips 60.

items.q: What is the lowest common multiple (LCM) of 3 and 4?
items.e: Multiples of 4: 4, 8, 12. Multiples of 3: 3, 6, 9, 12. The first number in both lists is 12. 3 and 4 share no factor except 1, so here the LCM is 3 × 4.

items.q: What is the LCM of 4 and 8?
items.e: Multiples of 8: 8. Multiples of 4: 4, 8. The first number in both lists is 8. 8 is a multiple of 4, so the bigger number is the LCM.

items.q: What is the LCM of 4 and 10?
items.e: Multiples of 10: 10, 20. Multiples of 4: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20. The first number in both lists is 20. 4 × 10 = 40 is a common multiple, but not the lowest.

items.q: What is the LCM of 6 and 10?
items.e: Multiples of 10: 10, 20, 30. Multiples of 6: 6, 12, 18, 24, 30. The first number in both lists is 30. 6 × 10 = 60 is a common multiple, but not the lowest.

items.q: What is the LCM of 5 and 7?
items.e: Multiples of 7: 7, 14, 21, 28, 35. Multiples of 5: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35. The first number in both lists is 35. 5 and 7 share no factor except 1, so here the LCM is 5 × 7.

items.q: What is the LCM of 8 and 10?
items.e: Multiples of 10: 10, 20, 30, 40. Multiples of 8: 8, 16, 24, 32, 40. The first number in both lists is 40. 8 × 10 = 80 is a common multiple, but not the lowest.

items.q: What is the LCM of 9 and 12?
items.e: Multiples of 12: 12, 24, 36. Multiples of 9: 9, 18, 27, 36. The first number in both lists is 36. 9 × 12 = 108 is a common multiple, but not the lowest.

items.q: Which list shows all the common factors of 12 and 18?
items.e: Factors of 12: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12. Factors of 18: 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18. Common factors: 1, 2, 3, 6. The highest is 6. Keep 1 and the highest common factor in the list, and use only numbers that divide both.

items.q: Which list shows all the common factors of 16 and 40?
items.e: Factors of 16: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16. Factors of 40: 1, 2, 4, 5, 8, 10, 20, 40. Common factors: 1, 2, 4, 8. The highest is 8. Keep 1 and the highest common factor in the list, and use only numbers that divide both.

items.q: Which list shows all the common factors of 24 and 36?
items.e: Factors of 24: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24. Factors of 36: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18, 36. Common factors: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12. The highest is 12. Keep 1 and the highest common factor in the list, and use only numbers that divide both.

items.q: Which number is a common factor of 36 and 54?
items.e: 9 × 4 = 36 and 9 × 6 = 54, so 9 is a common factor. 4 is a factor of 36 only, 27 is a factor of 54 only, and 108 is a common multiple.

items.q: Which number is a common factor of 42 and 60?
items.e: 6 × 7 = 42 and 6 × 10 = 60, so 6 is a common factor. 7 is a factor of 42 only, 10 is a factor of 60 only, and 420 is a common multiple.

items.q: Which number is not a common factor of 48 and 80?
items.e: 6 is a factor of 48, but 80 ÷ 6 = 13 remainder 2, so 6 is not a common factor. 2, 8 and 16 divide both numbers.

items.q: Which number is not a common factor of 60 and 90?
items.e: 4 is a factor of 60, but 90 ÷ 4 = 22 remainder 2, so 4 is not a common factor. 5, 6 and 15 divide both numbers.

items.q: What is the highest common factor (HCF) of 14 and 21?
items.e: Factors of 14: 1, 2, 7, 14. Factors of 21: 1, 3, 7, 21. Common factors: 1, 7. The highest is 7. 2 is a factor of 14 only, so it is not a common factor.

items.q: What is the HCF of 20 and 30?
items.e: Factors of 20: 1, 2, 4, 5, 10, 20. Factors of 30: 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 10, 15, 30. Common factors: 1, 2, 5, 10. The highest is 10. 5 is a common factor too, but not the highest.

items.q: What is the HCF of 18 and 27?
items.e: Factors of 18: 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18. Factors of 27: 1, 3, 9, 27. Common factors: 1, 3, 9. The highest is 9. 3 is a common factor too, but not the highest.

items.q: What is the HCF of 13 and 52?
items.e: Factors of 13: 1, 13. Factors of 52: 1, 2, 4, 13, 26, 52. Common factors: 1, 13. The highest is 13. 13 divides 52 (13 × 4 = 52), so the smaller number is the HCF.

items.q: What is the HCF of 9 and 20?
items.e: Factors of 9: 1, 3, 9. Factors of 20: 1, 2, 4, 5, 10, 20. Common factors: 1. The highest is 1. 9 and 20 share no factor except 1, so their HCF is 1.

items.q: What is the HCF of 28 and 42?
items.e: Factors of 28: 1, 2, 4, 7, 14, 28. Factors of 42: 1, 2, 3, 6, 7, 14, 21, 42. Common factors: 1, 2, 7, 14. The highest is 14. 7 is a common factor too, but not the highest.

items.q: What is the HCF of 48 and 72?
items.e: Factors of 48: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 24, 48. Factors of 72: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 9, 12, 18, 24, 36, 72. Common factors: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24. The highest is 24. 12 is a common factor too, but not the highest.

items.q: What is the HCF of 36 and 90?
items.e: Factors of 36: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18, 36. Factors of 90: 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 9, 10, 15, 18, 30, 45, 90. Common factors: 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18. The highest is 18. 9 is a common factor too, but not the highest.

items.q: What is the HCF of 54 and 81?
items.e: Factors of 54: 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18, 27, 54. Factors of 81: 1, 3, 9, 27, 81. Common factors: 1, 3, 9, 27. The highest is 27. 9 is a common factor too, but not the highest.

items.q: Hauwa says the HCF of 30 and 45 is 5, because 5 is a factor of both. Is she right?
items.e: 5 is a common factor, but not the highest. 15 × 2 = 30 and 15 × 3 = 45, so the HCF is 15. 90 is the LCM, and 30 is not a factor of 45.

items.q: Ifeoma says the HCF of 16 and 48 is 16. Is she right?
items.e: 16 × 3 = 48, so 16 is a factor of both numbers, and no factor of 16 is bigger than 16. The HCF can be the smaller number.

items.q: Which pair of numbers has only 1 as a common factor?
items.e: Factors of 8: 1, 2, 4, 8. Factors of 15: 1, 3, 5, 15. The only common factor is 1, so the answer is 8 and 15. 9 and 15 share 3, 8 and 14 share 2, and 12 and 15 share 3.

items.q: Which pair of numbers has a highest common factor of 6?
items.e: 18 = 6 × 3 and 24 = 6 × 4, and 3 and 4 share no factor except 1, so the HCF is 6. The HCF of 12 and 24 is 12, of 24 and 36 is 12, and 2 × 3 = 6 but the HCF of 2 and 3 is 1.

items.q: Two school bells ring together at 8:00 a.m. One rings every 15 minutes and the other every 8 minutes. After how many minutes will they next ring together?
items.e: We need the lowest common multiple of 15 and 8: 120 minutes.

items.q: Two school bells ring together at 8:00 a.m. One rings every 8 minutes and the other every 4 minutes. After how many minutes will they next ring together?
items.e: We need the lowest common multiple of 8 and 4: 8 minutes.

items.q: Two school bells ring together at 8:00 a.m. One rings every 15 minutes and the other every 9 minutes. After how many minutes will they next ring together?
items.e: We need the lowest common multiple of 15 and 9: 45 minutes.

items.q: Biscuits come in packets of 11 and drinks come in packs of 9. What is the smallest number of each you can buy so that you have the same number of biscuits and drinks?
items.e: LCM of 11 and 9 = 99.

items.q: Two school bells ring together at 8:00 a.m. One rings every 7 minutes and the other every 13 minutes. After how many minutes will they next ring together?
items.e: We need the lowest common multiple of 7 and 13: 91 minutes.

items.q: Biscuits come in packets of 6 and drinks come in packs of 14. What is the smallest number of each you can buy so that you have the same number of biscuits and drinks?
items.e: LCM of 6 and 14 = 42.

items.q: Two school bells ring together at 8:00 a.m. One rings every 3 minutes and the other every 9 minutes. After how many minutes will they next ring together?
items.e: We need the lowest common multiple of 3 and 9: 9 minutes.

items.q: Biscuits come in packets of 11 and drinks come in packs of 4. What is the smallest number of each you can buy so that you have the same number of biscuits and drinks?
items.e: LCM of 11 and 4 = 44.

items.q: Two school bells ring together at 8:00 a.m. One rings every 12 minutes and the other every 10 minutes. After how many minutes will they next ring together?
items.e: We need the lowest common multiple of 12 and 10: 60 minutes.

items.q: Two school bells ring together at 8:00 a.m. One rings every 15 minutes and the other every 3 minutes. After how many minutes will they next ring together?
items.e: We need the lowest common multiple of 15 and 3: 15 minutes.

items.q: Usman has 15 red beads and 21 blue beads. He wants to make bags with the same number of red beads and the same number of blue beads in each bag, with none left over. What is the greatest number of bags he can make?
items.e: We need the highest common factor of 15 and 21: 3 bags.

items.q: Uju has 24 red beads and 28 blue beads. She wants to make bags with the same number of red beads and the same number of blue beads in each bag, with none left over. What is the greatest number of bags she can make?
items.e: We need the highest common factor of 24 and 28: 4 bags.

items.q: Ikenna has 50 red beads and 30 blue beads. He wants to make bags with the same number of red beads and the same number of blue beads in each bag, with none left over. What is the greatest number of bags he can make?
items.e: We need the highest common factor of 50 and 30: 10 bags.

items.q: Yusuf has 12 red beads and 21 blue beads. He wants to make bags with the same number of red beads and the same number of blue beads in each bag, with none left over. What is the greatest number of bags he can make?
items.e: We need the highest common factor of 12 and 21: 3 bags.

items.q: Ada has 60 red beads and 70 blue beads. She wants to make bags with the same number of red beads and the same number of blue beads in each bag, with none left over. What is the greatest number of bags she can make?
items.e: We need the highest common factor of 60 and 70: 10 bags.

items.q: Amaka has 33 red beads and 22 blue beads. She wants to make bags with the same number of red beads and the same number of blue beads in each bag, with none left over. What is the greatest number of bags she can make?
items.e: We need the highest common factor of 33 and 22: 11 bags.

items.e: We need the highest common factor of 33 and 77: 11 bags.

items.e: We need the highest common factor of 75 and 45: 15 bags.

items.e: We need the highest common factor of 91 and 52: 13 bags.

items.q: Yusuf has 70 red beads and 60 blue beads. He wants to make bags with the same number of red beads and the same number of blue beads in each bag, with none left over. What is the greatest number of bags he can make?
items.e: We need the highest common factor of 70 and 60: 10 bags.
